title: A Thorn for the Choir
premise: Ines Ishikawa, a cartographer who maps realms that officially do not exist, has hidden his gift for three years in the magic-outlawed city of Vell. When the crown's witch-hunt sweeps him up, he discovers his sister's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain as payment for the city's founding charter — and that the hunt itself is a harvest to feed that court's hunger. Ines must ally with a disgraced inquisitor and a choir of smuggled singers whose voices can open the mountain's gates, racing against the solstice when sold souls are consumed forever. He trades his own gift — and his name from every map he ever drew — to buy her back, choosing truth over loyalty to the crown that made him invisible.
about_author: J. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people erased by institutions, drawing on their love of old maps and half-burned records.

chapters.title: The Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines Ishikawa's POV. Ines sells charms disguised as trinkets while secretly mapping the Veilways, unmapped realms only he can perceive. The crown's heralds post the Edict of Ash: all gifted persons must surrender themselves or be hunted. A raid burns his shop, and among the ashes he finds a ledger showing his missing sister's name sold 'to the court beneath.' Emotional beat: quiet dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Choir of Smuggled Voices
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Ines and Serah Duvane, an inquisitor who refused to hunt children and was cast out. Serah shelters Ines with the Choir — smugglers whose enchanted singing opens sealed ways into the mountain court. Ines learns the hunt is a soul-harvest feeding the court beneath, and the solstice consumption is weeks away. Emotional beat: wary alliance; trust kindling between enemies of the same law.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Owes
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with interludes from his sister Mira inside the court. Descending through the Veilways, the party discovers the founding charter was a contract signed in souls — including their parents'. The court offers Ines Mira's freedom in exchange for his cartographer's gift, which could map it new conquests. Betrayed by a Choir member loyal to the crown, they're captured at the threshold. Emotional beat: temptation and betrayal at the peak of despair.

chapters.title: The Unmapping
chapters.summary: Full ensemble POV during the solstice rite. Ines pretends to accept the bargain, then uses his gift to unmap the court itself — erasing its claim on every soul it holds, including Mira's, as the Choir sings the gates open. The cost: his gift, his name from every map, and Serah's life holding the door. Above ground, the Edict collapses without its hidden engine. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into justice outside the law, and a sister walking home.
